## 2026-10-21: Gibbon vtable +0x19c / +0x1a0 read: nothing to port

The "unread" slots in the Gibbon entry were mislabelled: the vtable is at 0x00b05740 (ctor 0x00564aa6), and 0x00568b70 / 0x00568bb4 are slots **+0x1ac / +0x1b0**. The real +0x19c / +0x1a0 are the base Enemy's 0x00520638 / 0x005218d4, shared by every enemy (13 / 158 call sites over the exe):
- +0x19c (0x00520638, `ret 4`, a position pointer argument): looks up the floor node under that position (vtable +0x1a4 = 0x00520b44, which searches the node list at +0x128) and, when found, caches its +0xc / +0x10 / +0x14 into +0x250..+0x258; copies the current position (+0x38 / +0x3c / +0x40) into the previous one (+0x44 / +0x48 / +0x4c); stores the new x / z (+0x38 / +0x40) from the argument (y is not written); clears +0x38c.
- +0x1a0 (0x005218d4, no argument): the same node cache from the current position (vtable +0x40 = 0x007712e0), the current-to-previous copy and the +0x38c clear, but no new position.
+0x38c looks like a timer (set to 0x96 in several places, about 480 references); what it times was not traced. These are generic movement bookkeeping, not Gibbon AI; the port keeps no previous-position / node cache / +0x38c timer.

+0x1ac (0x00568b70) and +0x1b0 (0x00568bb4) both start with 0x0051f814, which tests the entity against the global at 0x00a727a4. That global is set non-zero only at 0x004f88c7, inside 0x004f84b8, the mode-1 handler of the exe's **set editor** object (vtable 0x00afe1d8, ctor 0x004fb61c; strings "GROUP ENEMY SETEDITOR", "TOTAL BLOCK : %03d"); every other write stores 0. All 37 / 29 call sites of +0x1ac / +0x1b0 go through the same gate. +0x1ac re-runs the set-params routine (0x00564e98), moves the Gibbon between groups if its group index (+0x46c) changed (leave 0x00564720 / join 0x00564fa0) and resets the home point from the current position (0x00564fb4: +0x300 / +0x308 and +0x74 / +0x7c = x / z, +0x304 = y + 10); +0x1b0 prints "GROUP:%2d" and the other state fields as debug text. Both only run for the entity the set editor picked: a developer tool, not ported. ASSUMED: the set editor is never built in a retail session (its ctor is referenced only from a data table at 0x009b9214 with no code reference found; not proven).

## 2026-10-21: Mericarol flag 0x440 & 0x400: rare roll, never read for the Mericarol

The Mericarol ctor clears +0x440 (0x572c9c) and then rolls `call 0x007751b0` at 0x00572ca6 (a uniform float in [0, 1) from the 55-entry subtractive RNG 0x00763498) against the float at 0x00a73f24 (`fcomp`, `ja 0x572cca` skips the `or`). That float is 0 in the file and set to 0.002 (`0x3b03126f`) by the static initialiser at 0x00573618. So the `or 0x400` runs when roll <= 0.002: about 1 Mericarol in 500 gets the bit. The bit 0x10 and 0x08 readers of the same field (0x573060 / 0x5732c6 / 0x573390) are the Mericarol's own state flags, already ported.

Readers of 0x400: the only test of bit 0x400 after a +0x440 load in the whole .text is `test esi, 0x400` at 0x005593b4, inside 0x00559334 (frame 0x15c). (An earlier search used spaces where objdump prints a tab and wrongly found no caller.) 0x00559334 is called once, at 0x0055a9b3, by the state dispatcher 0x0055a95c (`jmp [4*eax+0x009252ac]` on states 0..9), which is vtable slot +0x164 (the AI state handler) of the class with vtable 0x00b04cc0 (ctor path 0x005585ee). The Mericarol's vtable is 0x00b06320, whose slot +0x164 is its own dispatcher 0x005710b8, so the reader never runs on a Mericarol: +0x440 is a per-class flag field, and the 0xb04cc0 class sets its own bits. Which enemy owns vtable 0x00b04cc0 was not identified.

Result: the Mericarol's 0x400 bit is set and never read, so it changes nothing; the port keeps no 0x400 bit. Caveat: the reader search looked 30 instructions back from each 0x400 test; a copy through a stack slot would not be caught.

## 2026-10-21: player movement: slowed / flag tie traced (exe)

The speed multipliers are in `legSpeed` (`render/playermove.ts`, 0.5 slowed, 0.75 for a flag). The exe function is 0x006978a0 (thiscall, `this` = player + 0x6b8, stack args: the player and the base float, `ret 8`):
- x *= 0.5 (`0x0093ca20`) when 0x00690344(player) is non-zero: that returns `[player+0x30] & 8`, but only when 0x0068a3fc(player) passes, i.e. `[player+0x3ec]` is NOT one of {0, 15, 18, 45} (table 0x0097f1c8, scanned by 0x00807d8c). So the 0.5 gate is bit 8 of +0x30 gated by a state field, not a plain slow flag.
- else x *= 0.75 (`0x0093ca24`) when bit 0x08 of `[this+0xc]` = `[player+0x6c4]` is set. 0x0069ba18 writes that field: 0, then 8 when `[player+0x30] & 0x00100000`. Which state that +0x30 bit is was not traced; calling it `guard` is NOT supported.
- the result goes to `[player+0x6c0]` (read by the walk / run code at 0x006a1a45 and 0x006a2089); then, when `[player+0x68c] & 1`, it is multiplied again by the float `[player+0x690]` and returned. The port has no such extra multiplier.

Callers (direct calls; an earlier search used spaces where objdump prints a tab and wrongly found none): 0x0069788c (base = global float `[0x00a94300]`) at 0x00697896 and 0x00697914 at 0x00697921; 0x0069788c is called from 0x00697881 and from 0x0069bad5 (inside 0x0069babc, reached from the poll 0x0069b93c -> 0x0069ba18), 0x00697914 from the walk / run update at 0x006a1a1d (base `[0x00a94324]`).

Port: the `slowed ? 0.5 : guard ? 0.75` order matches, but both conditions are named on guesses and the `[player+0x690]` factor is missing. Nothing sets `PlayerMover.slowed` / `guard` and the lobby has no status effects, so this changes nothing yet. Open: the meaning of `+0x30` bits 0x08 / 0x00100000, `+0x3ec`, and `+0x68c` / `+0x690`.

## 2026-10-21: Create a PARTY: wrong difficulty names (unitxt group 11 shift), first Playwright test

**Bug** (user: the party creation had no Normal and went back to the lobby). The Difficulty list showed "Hard / Very Hard / Ultimate / View the board": the classic client reads `unitxt_e.prs` from Ephinea's `data.gsl`, whose group 11 lacks entry 0xed ("Send to GM"), so every group 11 entry from 0xed on sits one index lower than PsoBB.exe asks for (0x139 "Challenge" instead of Play Mode "Normal", 0x13d "Hard" instead of Difficulty "Normal", 0x135 "Episode I" instead of the Meseta text). The loose `unitxt_j.prs` of the client data and newserv's bb-v4 `unitxt_e.prs` line up with the exe. Groups 0x00..0xec are the same in both files; groups 1 / 3 (items) differ a lot, so the whole file is not swapped.

**Fix:** `charcreate_text.ts` `menuTextAligned` (group 11 0x139 and 0x13d are the same non-empty word, as the exe's Play Mode list 0x00734578 and Difficulty list 0x00734628 need) and `withAlignedMenuText` (group 11 from the first aligned alternative); `classic/main.ts` loads unitxt once (`loadUnitxt`) and takes group 11 from `unitxt_j.prs` when the first file's is misaligned. This also fixes the other group 11 texts from 0xed on (Meseta, episode / mode names, area map help, team points).

**Level and difficulty** (exe, read by a subagent and checked here): the window does NOT filter difficulties by level. The difficulty list 0x00734628 always adds 0x13d / 0x13e / 0x13f (Normal, Hard, Very Hard) and adds 0x140 (Ultimate) when the window's mode `[this+0x20]` is 1, 2 or 3; the three constructions at 0x0079a777 / 0x0079a7f6 / 0x0079a858 pass 2, 3 and 1 (Episode 2, 4, 1), so Ultimate is always there. No level is read in the window's code. The level rule is the server's: newserv answered "You must be level 20 or above to play this difficulty." for Hard with a new character. Play Mode Challenge greys the Difficulty row (0x00734608), as `CreatePartyWindow.selectable` already did. The return to the lobby after creating a party is by design: `partyHost.back` leaves the game because the classic client has no field scene yet.

**Playwright:** `client/playwright.config.ts` and `client/e2e/party-create.spec.ts` (README in `client/e2e/`): log in, stand on the counter, Organize PARTY -> Create a PARTY -> EPISODE 1, check the Play Mode and Difficulty texts at the exe's indices, register a Normal party, expect the "entered game ... back to the lobby" log. Passes against local newserv. `npm ci` was also needed in `client/` (the @capacitor packages were declared but not installed, which broke `classic.html` under Vite).

**Checks:** `npx playwright test` (1 passed), `tests/gamelist.test.ts` (new: group 11 alignment), `items`, `options`, `teammenu`, `fieldhud`, `warpmenu`, client `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## 2026-10-21: Gibbles concealed while hidden, Epsilon tech immunity applied

**What changed:** a hidden Gibbles is now concealed like the other hidden enemies. `GibblesAi` has an `untargetable` getter (state 0 / 1, and the held drop-in: `dormant` or `arrive` below `arriveHold`), and its frame sets `out.hidden` from that same getter. `render/combat.ts` `concealed()` lists `GibblesAi`, so it is off the radar, lock-on, technique targeting and confused-enemy targeting while hidden. Invulnerable Epsilon keeps the existing "0" path in `applyEnemyHit`. The exe's `EpsigardProcessTechHit_0055aa5c` is only described as "blocks"; no number or effect is mirrored, so none is shown. The comment in `combat/enemyfsmep2d.ts` no longer says the owner does not apply it.

## 2026-10-21: player leg speed: the 0.5 / 0.75 conditions identified

Follow-up of "player movement: slowed / flag tie traced" (a Haiku subagent traced it, the decisive writes and constants were checked here). In 0x006978a0:
- **0.5 = slowed outside the hubs.** Bit 0x08 of player+0x30 is the slow status: `slow_entity` (0x00778b10) writes `(flags & ~0x3c) | 8` at 0x00778bc6 (the slot value 0x11 = `STATUS.slow`, 0xd2 frames). 0x00690344 applies it only when 0x0068a3fc passes, i.e. the map id at player+0x3ec is not in {0, 15, 18, 45} (table 0x0097f1c8: Pioneer 2 Ep1, lobby, Pioneer 2 Ep2, Pioneer 2 Ep4). So the slow does not slow you in the hubs.
- **0.75 = guard stance.** Bit 0x00100000 of player+0x30 (the Ghidra enum's `in_guard_stance`; newserv calls the same flag "near enemy"), copied to player+0x6c4 bit 0x08 by 0x0069ba18. 0x0052ac5c sets / clears it by the distance to the player's target (0x00770738) with hysteresis: hunters enter within 50 (d^2 2500, 0x00922334) and leave beyond 100 (10000, 0x00922330); other classes 100 / 150 (0x0092233c / 0x00922338); no target clears it (0x0052ad36), a target id >= 0x1000 sets it (0x0052ad28). 0x006a29f4 also sets it (with a velocity reset) at the end of the light-hit and evade states, and the 6x3E / 6x3F / 6x40 handlers copy it from the packet for remote players (0x00698cb6 / 0x00698db5).
- **[player+0x690]**: 0.4 by default (the player ctor), part of the scale block the quest opcode `set_shrink_size` writes; the gate player+0x68c bit 0 is only ever written 0 in player code, so the factor is inert in normal play.

So the port's names `slowed` / `guard` are right after all (the earlier entry doubted `guard`); the hub exemption of the slow and the stance's proximity rule are not ported (`PlayerMover` is only driven in the lobby, where neither applies). `render/playermove.ts` header updated. Unverified details: the 0x006898cc proximity writer (2500 / 3600) and which handlers call 0x006a29f4 (taken from the dump's names).

## 2026-10-21: dead Gibbles sinks for 250 frames

Exe (PsoBB.exe, Ephinea 1.25.13): the Gibbles death state is the state 9 handler at 0x005606d4 (the dispatcher 0x0056021c calls it for enemy+0x32e = 9). Its own sub-state is the word at enemy+0x330, which the handler switches on:
- sub 0 (0x005607c0): `enemy+0x3a8 = 0`, sub := 1, then the call 0x00772b44 (the death motion, row 9 = motion 2, 0.7).
- sub 1 (0x0056074c): calls 0x007aa094 (the animation update), then waits for the play-once motion to end (`test byte [edi+0xb0], 0x10`, 0x00560759). Nothing moves until then.
- transition, on the tick the motion ends (0x0056075d): sub := 4, the call 0x00782b64 on (0, 0, -10) with the heading at +0x60 (a point 10 units behind), 0x00578148 with 10 (0x005607a7), the particle helper 0x00578778 with id 0x46 (0x005607b3). No sink on this tick.
- sub 4 (0x00560706..0x0056071a), every game tick: `y(+0x3c) -= 0.1` (float at 0x00925b04 = 0.10000000149), then `v(+0x3a8) += 0.1` (the same constant), and if the new velocity is above 25.0 (0x00925b00) sub := 3 (0x00560720), else stays in sub 4.
- sub 3 (0x00560731): `word [edi+0x8] |= 1` (0x00560743). The removal flag. The sweep that deletes the entity is not in this handler (UNCLEAR which pass reads that bit, and its order within the frame).

The timing follows from the float steps: simulating the exe's float32 operations gives the 250th sink tick as the first one with a velocity above 25 (25.0000591), so the sink is 250 game ticks of 0.1 (25 units total, y -25.00006), and the flag is set on the 251st tick after the motion ends.

Constants: `GIBBLES.sinkStep = fr(0.1)` (0x00925b04), `GIBBLES.sinkLimit = 25` (0x00925b00). Not hidden: the handler writes no hide or untargetable flag (`+0xb0` is only read). The dead entity is excluded from hits and the minimap by its `dead` flag, as before.

**What changed:** `GibblesAi` (`client/src/combat/enemyfsmep2a.ts`) overrides `kill()` to start the sink, and has `tickDead(animationEnded)`, which is one game tick of sub 1 / 4 / 3. Its `lift` getter is now `yOff + sink`, and `removed` is true from the tick after the sink. `render/combat.ts` no longer lets the death-state removal take a Gibbles (`!(e.ai instanceof GibblesAi)` on the `dropDead` line in the death loop). `tickEnemies` runs `tickGibblesSink` for a dead Gibbles every game tick, instead of skipping it as a dead enemy: it calls `tickDead`, moves the model to the ground plus the brain's lift (the same ground call as a live enemy), and drops the enemy when `removed`. The removal is the only owner-side change; the other enemies keep their paths.

**Not ported:** the death particle (0x00578778, id 0x46), the sound call (0x00578148, 10) and the point (0x00782b64) from the transition tick. The helpers are not named in any reference we have, so the ids and sounds are UNCLEAR and nothing is played. Gi Gue's death particles stay open.

ASSUMED / UNCLEAR: the sink is relative to the floor (the exe's +0x3c is the absolute y, the port keeps the floor by the owner's ground call, so the drop is applied on top of it); the 250-tick count assumes one `tickDead` per game tick (the owner's 30 ticks a second); the removal tick is taken as the sub 3 tick, the exact sweep order is UNCLEAR; the particle and sound ids above.

**Checks:** `tests/enemyfsmep2a.test.ts` (the sink timeline: the motion runs out with no sink, 0.1 on the first tick, 10 units at tick 100, 24.9 at 249, 25 at 250, removal exactly on tick 251, the sink stops after it; the constants), `tests/combat.test.ts` (needs the newserv data under `vendor/`), client `tsc --noEmit` clean.

Not run in Chrome.

## 2026-10-21: Saint-Milion missiles

**Outcome: not ported (stopped after reading the exe, as the brief allows).** The missile is a model-driven object, not a straight shot: its flight, its end and its damage go through the motion system, a vector library and an explosion routine that the port does not have. No code changed; `docs/HANDOFF.md` item 4 still lists the missiles as events only.

**Where they come from.** Row 18 of `SM_STATES` (0x009f6c60 + 18 * 40, the state 0x12 row of `saintmilionboss.ts`) has handler 0x0076966c. It dispatches phase 4 to 0x0076b8f4 and phase 0 to 0x0076968c:
```
76966c: cmp eax, 0x4 / jne 76967d / call 0x76b8f4 / ret     ; phase 4
76967d: test eax, eax / jne 769686 / call 0x76968c          ; phase 0
```
- **Entry (0x0076b8f4):** one object: `push 0xe4 / call 0x5caba4` (allocation of 0xE4 bytes), then the constructor 0x0076619c with the boss's id word (`movzx eax, [ebx+0x394]`, no offset) and target 0x27 (`call 0x768964`).
- **Phase 0 (0x0076968c):** `call 0x7aaa30` with the float 5.0 (0x40a00000, a motion check on the boss's model: flags at +0xb0), then `cmp [ebx+0xf80], 3 / 4`. `+0xf80` is the arena index (see `saintmilionboss.ts`, `arena`), so the two missiles come only in arenas 3 and 4 (the centre arenas, range 620). They are built with id word + 2 (target 0x27) and id word + 3 (target 0x28).
- So the exe makes 1 missile on entry and 2 more on phase-0 frames in those arenas. **UNCLEAR:** how often the phase-0 branch runs them (the gate is tested every frame; the rest of 0x007aaa30 was not read, so it may be an "exactly at frame 5" test).

**The object.** Constructor 0x0076619c (args: `[owner+0x3cc]`, `[owner+0x60]`, a position pointer (`owner+0xdd4` / `+0xe14`, or 0), 0xa9b078, the id). vtable 0x00b434b8: +0 0x007660c4, +4 0x00766384 (the base update 0x00765a40, the owner's position from `[this+0x60]+0x30..0x38`, then 0x007663d4 or 0x00766800). Fields: +0x30 a cycle timer (`fld 1.0` (0x00976198) added each frame, wraps at +0x34; `1.0` steps), +0x68 a frame counter, +0x6c the id, +0x70 a motion model (built with 0x007b4b48, 0x007b9a88), +0x74 an array of four children (0x0057739c, the stride 0x1c). The constructor reads a global counter (`[0xa9b008]`) and a table at 0x00976160.

**Per-frame (0x007663d4).**
- Lifetime: `cmp [this+0x68], 0xf0 / jg 0x766786`: 240 frames, then the kill path 0x007667a8 (`call 0x661448`, effect 0x6f7 via 0x00814298).
- The motion end test: `call 0x7b5290` with flag 0x80000 on the missile's model; when set, the explosion 0x007667e4 (`push 3; push 0x41f00000 (30.0); push &this+0x38; call 0x0076a724`: type 3, radius 30.0, at the missile) and then the kill 0x007667a8.
- A test `call 0x0077fffc` with the missile's position and the argument -1 (**UNCLEAR:** taken as a ray / target test from its position in the code; not read).
- The launch (0x0076681c) takes the owner's position and two normalised vectors (0x0082ddd8, 0x0082dcbc) scaled by 0x00976174 = **5.0**, into `+0x50` and `+0x58`. Its per-frame motion is then set by 0x007b52c4 / 0x007b52ec (model animation) and 0x007b5218 / 0x007b4c58 (node transforms).

**Constants read:** 0x00976174 = 5.0 (launch scale), 0x00976180 = 0.08, 0x00976184 = 1.2, 0x00976188 = 1.45, 0x0097618c = 0.1, 0x00976190 = 20.0, 0x00976198 = 1.0 (the timer step), 0x00976160 = 0 and 2^32 (unsigned bias). Lifetime 240, explosion type 3 radius 30.0, arenas 3 / 4, 1 + 2 missiles.

**Why it stops here.**
- The missile is animated through its model (0x7b5290, 0x7b52c4, 0x7b52ec, 0x7b5218, 0x7b4c58, 0x7b999c), and the port has no motion object for a shot. The 0x0076a724 explosion (the damage: type, radius and the entity call) and the player choice 0x00768964 / 0x00780d3c were not read.
- Hit radius, damage and the homing rule are not read: the code at 0x00766650 .. 0x00766700 moves the model, and the steering is not in 0x007663d4. **UNCLEAR:** whether the missile homes at all (the launch direction comes from the owner's position and a target, but the turn is not seen).

**Changes:** this entry only. The events stay in `combat/saintmilionboss.ts` (state 18 at phase 4, line ~630). No constants, tests or shots were added.

**Checks:** none run (docs only). Not run in Chrome.

## 2026-10-21: Gee pack states 6 / 10

**What changed:** nothing ported. The two states are unreachable for a Gee the factory makes, so `combat/enemyfsmep2a.ts` only gets comments: the note in the Gee section (replacing "not reproduced" with the entry paths) and one above `GeeState`. `docs/HANDOFF.md` to-do item 2 no longer lists them.

**The handlers:** dispatcher 0x0055d11c (`cmp eax, 0x12; ja`, `jmp [4*eax + 0x925500]`). Table entry 6 leads to `call 0x0055ebb8` (objdump: `55d1c2: call 0x55ebb8`), entry 10 to `call 0x0055d8d4` (`55d18f: call 0x55d8d4`). State 6 (0x0055ebb8): enter (arg 4) pushes 6, clears enemy+0xb8, clears 0x00400000 of enemy+0x3d0, calls the hit-box vtable +0x188, sets 0x01000000 of enemy+0x30 and enemy+0x43c = 0. Frame (arg 0): FindEnemyTarget 200 (0x00520ea0) and a sub-state machine (enemy+0x43c) that waits on the other pack members (flags 0x4 / 0x80000 / 0x200 of enemy+0x3d0). Transitions (arg 3) are left to vtable +0x1b8. State 10 (0x0055d8d4): enter pushes 10 and clears 0x00400000; frame turns toward the velocity and quantises the altitude, then the hover (`push 0x3f4ccccd`, the 0x00520adc hit check); transition: pushes 6 when vtable +0x1b8 returns 0 and the float at enemy+0x3b4 is below the constant at 0x00925730 (value not read). Both are the pack roles of an entity-group code path that a single Gee never takes (below). Not decoded further: UNCLEAR.

**What enters them (all the `push 6` / `push 10` sites inside the Gee code range 0x0055c974 .. 0x0055fb00):**
- `55c71f: push 6` in state 4's transition (0x0055c5f4, arg 3; the path at 0x0055c6e5): after the 0x00000002 flag of enemy+0x3d0 is cleared, `cmp dword [ebp+0x3cc], 1; je 55c71f` pushes 6, otherwise `push 5` (climb). So 6 needs enemy+0x3cc == 1.
- `55e9ff: push 10` in state 7's exit (0x0055e9e1): `test [eax+0x3d0], 0x00100000; je 55e9fd` pushes 10 when the flag is clear, `push 9` (strafe) when it is set.
- `55d95b: push 6` in state 10's transition (after `call [edx+0x1b8]` returns 0 and the float check at enemy+0x3b4 above).
No other Gee-range site pushes 6 or 10. The other callers of the setter 0x0051f62c with 6 / 10 belong to other families (their own objects).

**Why they are unreachable (the deciding values):**
1. enemy+0x3cc (the role the port calls the pack role) is written in the Gee range only at 0x0055ca28 (`mov dword [ecx+0x3cc], 0`, in the factory 0x0055c974, unconditionally). The factory takes no subtype argument; the other stores to 0x3cc in `.text` are in other families' constructors (e.g. 0x004367cd: 0x1e / 3 / 5 / 10 / 30, in an entity that is not a Gee). The base code at 0x0051f62c / 0x0051f664 / 0x00520ea0 / 0x00521410 / 0x005213ec does not write it.
2. So the alert transition never sees 1: 0x0055c71f is dead for a Gee. The Gee always climbs (state 5) after the alert.
3. The spawn sets the strafe flag: `55fa71: mov eax,[edi+0x3cc]; test; jne 55fa8e`, and for a role of 0 `55fa7b..55fa86: or eax, 0x00100000` on enemy+0x3d0. Nothing the Gee runs clears 0x00100000 (the masks `and ... 0xffefffff` in `.text` are in other families' code, e.g. 0x0044a526 clears enemy+0x390, not 0x3d0; the helpers the Gee calls, 0x0053e538 (sets 0x2), 0x0053fa2c (sets 0x8), 0x00520ea0 / 0x00521410 / 0x005213ec, do not clear it). So at the shoot's exit the test at `55e9e7` finds the flag set, takes 9, and 10 never runs. Its exit to 6 (`55d959`) is then dead as well.

So a Gee made by the factory cannot enter 6 or 10, whatever the set file says: the set parameters feed 0x100 (param1), 0x2000000 / 0x4000000 (param2), the speeds and the step, none of them 0x3cc or 0x100000. The port's `subtype` (`params[5]`, render/combat.ts:785) is not passed to `GeeAi` (render/combat.ts:852) and nothing in the Gee code reads it; the phrase "factory's subtype 0" in the 2026-10-20 entry is therefore wrong: the field is enemy+0x3cc, and it is always 0. The port's `ChooseAttack` also reads 0x3cc in the exe (0x0055c4cc: non-zero means shoot only, no melee): with 0 it is the shoot, shoot, melee pattern the port has.

**Checks:** `/usr/bin/objdump -d -M intel` over the whole `.text` (grep of `[reg+0x3cc]` stores, `0x100000` tests / sets, `0xffefffff` / `0xfeffffff` masks, and `call 0x51f62c` with the pushed value); the jump table read with `tools/exedata.py read 0x00925500 h`. The Ghidra dump is not on this machine (`tools/refsrc.sh` has no REFSRC checkout), so every name here is from the exe. No code change in the behaviour: `tests/enemyfsmep2a.test.ts` is unchanged and must still pass.

**ASSUMED:** (a) "Nothing the Gee runs writes enemy+0x3cc / 0x3d0" is checked over the functions the Gee calls and the whole `.text` store list by pattern, not by dataflow through the owner: the owner (`render/combat.ts`) and the packet code could in principle write the object's memory in another way, not checked; (b) a generic owner path that calls the Gee's setter with 6 or 10 is not visible from the Gee range (the owner calls the Gee through its vtable, as in the port); (c) the spawn's state 1 / 2 choice by 0x2000000 is taken from the port's reading (0x0055fa94), not from the set file. UNCLEAR: the exact states 6 / 10 frame details (the sub-state numbers 0..3 and the hover constants), which are not ported and so not tested.

**Left:** the states 6 / 10 themselves (if a later pass finds a writer of enemy+0x3cc or a clear of 0x00100000 for a Gee, port them from 0x0055ebb8 / 0x0055d8d4 with these notes as the start). Not run in Chrome.

## 2026-10-21: Gi Gue stomp entities

**Addresses:** the stomp is Gi Gue's prepare state (`0x0056a3cc`, sub-step 2,
after the motion frame test `fcomp [0x926324]` = 10). Its call sites in
`0x0056a3cc` (the prepare function; `0x0056a70c` before them is the cast flash,
visual only):

```
56a48d: call 0x6f1eb0   ; Zalure object: push [eax+0x20] (iparam3), push edi+0x300 x2, push edi
56a49d: call 0x6e7998   ; Jellen object, same arguments
```

- `0x6f1eb0` / `0x6e7998` are the `new` + constructor wrappers of two technique
  objects (0x14c bytes, `new` = 0x5caba4). Zalure: ctor 0x6f1f28, vtable
  0x00b3e770, tech 12 (`0x6ded14(12, level)`). Jellen: ctor 0x6e7a10, vtable
  0x00b3d850, tech 11 (`0x6e7bc4 push 0xb`).
- Position: `edi+0x300/0x304/0x308` is the entity's world position triple (the
  same block the enemy code reads elsewhere, e.g. 0x00501229), so the objects
  stand on Gi Gue. Level: the MovementData row 26 iparam3 (`g_GiGue_AnimSpeeds`
  +0x20).
- Update (vtable +4 = `0x6f2420`, Zalure; the Jellen one is the same shape): the
  owner is looked up by the id at +0xb4 (`0x007b4d18`), no owner = dead. The
  object has no target list (+0xec is 0 from the ctor), so it runs the area tick
  `AoE_TechDamageTick_006deadc`, which takes candidates from
  `AoE_TechCollisionCheck_006eb0e8` and tests each (`0x006ea71c`: word +0x96 == 1)
  then calls its hit slot (vtable +0x10 = `0x006f24c0`), which calls the target's
  vtable +0x60 with group 12 (Zalure) or 11 (Jellen): the debuff, no damage row.
  Last, `or word [+8], 1` ends the object: one tick, no lifetime.
- No knockback, no damage from an attack-data row: the stomp is a debuff only.

**Changes:** the stomp now hits every living player within
`techReach(TECH.zalure | TECH.jellen, level)` (range_h + 5, the port's AoE
reach; level 4 = 55, level 10 = 79) of Gi Gue's position, in XZ, strictly inside,
instead of the cone pick. Zalure is pushed first (creation order). The
prepare gate (sub 0: a player in the cone starts the prepare) is unchanged.

## 2026-10-21: Saint-Milion missiles, flight and explosion (not ported)

**Outcome: still not ported.** The flight is steered by the model's motion system, the explosion goes through a world object's vtable, and the damage rule was not reached, so per the brief nothing was added to `combat/saintmilionboss.ts`. `docs/HANDOFF.md` item 4 still lists the missiles as events only.

**The explosion (0x007667e4 -> 0x0076a724).** The missile's end path at 0x007667e4 is:
```
7667e4: push 0x0 / add ecx, 0x38 / push 0x41f00000 / push ecx / mov ecx, [0xa9b07c] / push 0x3 / call 0x76a724
```
So `0x76a724(type = 3, pos = this+0x38, radius = 30.0, flag = 0)`, thiscall on the global at 0x00a9b07c (a manager; set to 0 at 0x007675fa in the owner's clean-up).
- `0x76a724` calls `0x768990(type, out1, out2)` on the manager (`cmp eax, 9 / ja / jmp [4*eax + 0x9768c4]`). Type 3 goes to 0x00768a00: `mov eax, [ecx+0x3d0] / fild [eax+0x20] / mov eax, 0x40400000 (3.0)`, so the per-type value is the int at `[manager+0x3d0] + 0x20` times 3.0, written as `{0, float}` / `{1, int}` into the out pointers (0x00768a50 .. 0x00768a7a). The meaning of `[manager+0x3d0]` and of its +0x1c..+0x28 fields is **UNCLEAR**.
- Then, for type 0 the code calls `0x0051fdf8`, for any other type `0x0051fc9c`, both with `(pos, out, flag)`. Both compare a float constant (0x009216cc / 0x009216d4) with `[pos+8]` and call a vtable slot (+0x30 / +0x34, or +0x3c in 0x51fdf8) of the global world object at 0x00a72eb4. That object is written at 0x005219b4 (`mov [0xa72eb4], eax`), and its class and vtable were not identified. 0x0051fd44 then writes the record `[obj+0xa4]` with `+0x18 = 0x9d03`.
- **UNCLEAR:** who the vtable call damages, the hit shape (the radius 30.0 is passed on, not tested here), the attack's power / knockback, and whether the player is in range. The damage rule is therefore not ported.

**The flight (0x00766650 .. 0x00766700, inside the update 0x007663d4).** The missile's position is copied from `[edi+0x48]` / `[edi+0x4c]` into `[ebx+0x60]` / `[ebx+0x64]`, then read and written through the model's node calls (0x007b999c, 0x007b5218, 0x007b4c58). A float test against 0x00976190 (**20.0**) compares two values from the node position; when it passes, `call 0x007b52ec` with `push 0; push 4` sets motion state 4 on `[edi+0x70]` (the end of flight, which leads to the explosion once the 0x80000 flag of 0x007b5290 is set).
- So the path is driven by the model (keyframes or a node path, read by the engine's motion code), not by a vector the port can integrate. **ASSUMED** if ported: a straight line along the launch vector (5.0 per frame, 0x00976174), ended at 240 frames or when the model reaches the 20.0 test.
- **UNCLEAR:** homing. No steering was seen in 0x007663d4 or 0x00766650 .. 0x00766700; the player-choice calls 0x00768964 / 0x00780d3c and the test 0x0077fffc (its frame at 0x00780000 uses the globals 0x00a9bc84 and 0x00a9b500, not read to the end) were not decoded.

**Changes:** this entry only. No code, tests, shots or HANDOFF change.

**Checks:** `/usr/bin/objdump -d -M intel` over 0x0076a724 .. 0x0076a8c0, 0x007667d4 .. 0x00766800, 0x00768990 .. 0x00768a7a, 0x0051fc9c .. 0x0051fd44, 0x0051fdf8 .. 0x0051fe40, 0x00766650 .. 0x00766700 and 0x0077fffc .. 0x00780020; `tools/exedata.py read 0x009768c4 u 10` (the type jump table); `tools/exedata.py xref` on 0x00a72eb4 and 0x00a9b07c. ## 2026-10-21: Saint-Milion lasers

**Outcome: not ported (findings only, as the brief allows).** The lasers are two model-driven objects with a telegraph, a sweeping beam whose origin is read from a track of the boss, and a damage call through the shared attack dispatcher. Three of those links are not read well enough for a faithful port (listed under UNCLEAR). No code, test or constant changed. `docs/HANDOFF.md` item 4 still lists the lasers as events only.

**Where they come from.** States 0x13 and 0x14 (`SM_STATE` laserA / laserB, rows 19 and 20 of `SM_STATES`) share one handler, 0x007697dc (the table at 0x009f6c60 + 19 * 40 and + 20 * 40, handler word at +4 = 7772124 = 0x007697dc, the same word for both rows). The handler sends phase 4 to 0x0076b85c and phase 0 to 0x00769808:
```
7697dc: mov eax, [esp+4] / cmp eax, 4 / jne 7697ea / call 0x76b85c      ; phase 4
7697f0: cmp eax, 4 / je 769802 / test eax, eax / jne 769802 / call 0x769808 ; phase 0
```
The port's `case 19/20: events.push({name: 'laser'})` (saintmilionboss.ts, line ~630) is the phase-4 branch only.

**Phase 4 (0x0076b85c): the telegraph.** It allocates 0x60 bytes (`push 0x60 / call 0x5caba4`) and builds a different class (vtable 0x00b43410, ctor 0x00765c68 on the base 0x00765a14). Its argument is the boss's `+0xe94` (`lea eax, [ecx+0xe94]`), or 0 when `0x768964(42)` fails (the id range check, 0 .. 0x2a). The role is `[boss+0x3cc]`. **UNCLEAR:** what the telegraph draws and whether it hurts; its vtable and update were not read.

**Phase 0 (0x00769808): the beam, frames 27 and 28.**
- Frame 27 (`call 0x7aaa30` with 0x41d80000 = 27.0; 0x7aaa30 is the "the model's clock crossed this frame" test, the port's `clock.crossed`): `0x768964(42)` passes, `[boss+0xec4..0xecc]` is copied into a local point, and the effect 0x6f9 is spawned there (`call 0x814298`, push 1, 0, &point).
- Frame 28 (0x41e00000 = 28.0): if the clock crossed, the beam's type is chosen. Arena `[boss+0xf80]` 3 or 4: `0x7751b0 >= 0.5` gives type 3, else 2. Other arenas: `>= 0.5` gives 1, else 0 (0x9773c8 = 0.5). `0x7751b0` is a turn fraction in [0, 1) of the object at `boss+0x168` (0x763498, the upper 16 bits over 0x978234); when the state is 10 it uses 0x8587a5 / 0x978230 instead. **UNCLEAR:** what the 0x168 object is (it is probably the boss's facing in its own frame).
- Then the origin (`call 0x579de0` with 0x41e80000 = 29.0, on `[0xa9b080 + 4 * [0x9f75c8 + 8 * [0xa9b078]]]`), the point is transformed by 0x82eab8 and the beam object is built: alloc 0x60, `push type / push [boss+0x60] / push point / push [boss+0x3cc] / call 0x76cb9c`.
- So each cast makes one telegraph (phase 4) and one beam (frame 28). The port queues 0x13 or 0x14 from the stomp (state 17, `queue(rand < 0.5 ? 0x13 : 0x14)`); that link was not checked in the exe.

**The beam object (ctor 0x0076cb9c, vtable 0x00b43b60).** Arguments: role, origin point, owner `[boss+0x60]`, type. Base ctor 0x00765a14 (the same base as the missile). Fields: `+0x30` a cycle clock stepping 1.0 (`0x977a08`) and wrapping at `+0x34`; `+0x34` = frames of the motion - 1 (`fild [motion+4]`, `0x977a0c` = -1.0); `+0x38 .. +0x40` the point; `+0x50` the owner; `+0x54` an angle (BAMS, starts at 0); `+0x58` a ramp; `+0x5c` the type.

**Per frame (vtable +4, 0x0076ccdc).**
- `+0x58 = min(+0x58 + 0.025, 1.0)` (`0x9779f8`, `0x977a08`): a 40-frame ramp.
- Angle: `+0x54 += step[type]`, with the table at 0x009779b8 (12 bytes per type: u32 step, float rate, float amplitude):

| type | step (BAMS) | rate (+0x40 = angle * rate) | amplitude (+0x38 = amplitude * sin(angle)) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 728 | 0.00213623 | -140 |
| 1 | 728 | 0.00213623 | +140 |
| 2 | 280 | 0.00717163 | -300 |
| 3 | 280 | 0.00717163 | +300 |

  The sine is `0x82dcbc`, a table lookup at `0x00989560` indexed by `(angle >> 4) & 0xfff` with the quadrant fix-ups. Type bit 1 (2 / 3) is the arena 3 / 4 "long" beam, bit 0 the sweep direction. `+0x40` is the linear term as written (`fild [edi+0x54]; fmul [rate]`): the port should follow the exe here, not a circle.
- The point goes through the owner's frame: `0x82d8bc` (owner `[+0x50]`, the transform), `0x82eab8` (the matrix on `+0x38`), `0x82da80`, `0x82ebac`. **UNCLEAR:** the exact matrix chain (only the first two were read).
- Hit: `push 0x16ef / push &+0x38 / call 0x780630`. `0x780630` walks the 256-entry list at `[0xaab3f0] + 0x20` (the `0xa9b500` records), with a flag mask test (`[rec+0x14] & 0x16ef`) and a circle test in x / z (`(x - rec.x)^2 + (z - rec.z)^2 <= rec.r^2`, `rec` at +0x4 / +0xc / +0x10). On a hit the record's entity id goes to `+0x3c` (`mov [edi+0x3c], ebp`) and the damage call runs: `call 0x76a724` with type 5, the point, and the radius `+0x58 * 64` (`0x9779f4`). The type-5 case of 0x768990 (table 0x009768c4, entry 5 = 0x007689df) is `fild [attack+0x28]` (the attacker's `+0x3d0` record, the global `[0xa9b07c]`), radius 10.0 (`mov eax, 0x41200000` from the same case), then `0x51fdf8` / `0x51fc9c` deal the damage. Effect 0x6fa at the point (`call 0x8144b0`).
- On a miss the word `[+0x8]` gets `or 0xffff0001`. **UNCLEAR:** whether this kills the beam or only marks the frame; the end of the beam (the base 0x765a40 and the motion end) was not read.

**Why it is not ported.**
1. The beam's origin is a motion track: `0x579de0` returns a sample index from an object's start / end / length (+0xc, +0x10, +0x14), and the object comes from `[0xa9b080]` through the global `[0xa9b078]` and the table 0x009f75c8. The port has no such object for the boss.
2. The beam's lifetime and end (0x765a40 and the motion end flag) and the `+0x8` flag are unread.
3. The damage's attacker `[0xa9b07c]` (its `+0x3d0` record, `+0x28`) and the damage / knockback path 0x51fdf8 are unread, so the damage row is not known.
4. The telegraph (0x765c68, vtable 0x00b43410) is unread.

**ASSUMED (none ported, so none in code).** The sweep numbers above are the exe's; the port would have to pick the origin, the lifetime and the damage row, which is where the approximations would go.

**Changes:** this entry only. `docs/HANDOFF.md` item 4 keeps "lasers" (still events only).

**Checks:** none run (docs only). Not run in Chrome.

## 2026-10-21: Jellen / Zalure area of an enemy cast

**Addresses:**
- Objects: Zalure ctor `0x006f1eb0` (ctor `0x006f1f28`, vtable `0x00b3e770`, tech 12) and Jellen `0x006e7998` (ctor `0x006e7a10`, vtable `0x00b3d850`, tech 11). Each copies the row's `range_h` into `+0x90`: `0x006ded14(tech, level, 0xffff)` returns the row, `mov eax, [row+8]` / `mov [ebx+0x90], edx` (Jellen `0x006e7bdc`, Zalure `0x006f20f7`). Dword 2 of the row is `range_h`, as `techData` reads it.
- The probe: the object's `+0xe8` is a probe struct P. The ctor sets `Q = [P+0xa4]` and `[Q+0xc] = [obj+0x90]` (`mov edx,[edx+0xa4]` / `mov [edx+0xc],eax`, `0x006e7ac7`..`0x006e7ad3`; Zalure `0x006f1fdf`..`0x006f1feb`). So the probe radius is `range_h`. P's centre is the object's position (`0x006eb1e1`..`0x006eb1e7` copy `obj+0x20..0x28` into `P+0x38..0x40`).
- Callers: the Gi Gue stomp (`0x0056a48d`, `0x0056a49d`) and Sinow Zoa's cast (`0x005932b2`, `0x005932d0`, inside `SinowzoaExecuteSpecialTech_00593268` by address) use the same two ctors. The area tick `AoE_TechDamageTick_006deadc` calls `AoE_TechCollisionCheck_006eb0e8` when `[obj+0xe8]` is set (`0x006eb354` otherwise), then for each candidate `0x006ea71c` (word `+0x96 == 1`) and the object's vtable `+0x10` with `[obj+0xb8]` = the candidate's hit box.
- Candidates, `0x006eb0e8`:
  - Caster type (word `+0x1c`) >= 4 (an enemy): the four player slots `0x007b4d18(0..3)`, each of another type with `+0x30 & 0x10000000`. Path `0x006eb2af`.
  - Caster type < 4 (a player): the entity array `0x00aad720` (count `0x00aae16c`), each of another type with `+0x30 & 0x30000000`. A player target (type < 4) also needs the caster's `+0x3f0`; enemies skip that test (`0x006eb22c`..`0x006eb23d`).
  - Each goes through `0x007b65b4(P, target, 10000.0f)`: not the same entity, no flag `0x800` / `0x80000800`; the XZ distance squared (`0x007a9180`, `dx^2 + dz^2`) must not exceed 10000 (XZ <= 100, the `fcompp` / `jb` at `0x007b65fb`..`0x007b6604`); both `+0xa4` pointers non-null; then the overlap `0x007b5318` of P's box against the target's hit boxes.
  - The count is capped at 15: the 16th candidate sets the count to 15 (`0x006eb32e`, `0x006eb33d`). A side list `0xaad6e0` (eight slots, `0x007b686f`) is written after the overlap and does not change the result as far as read.
- Constants: `10000.0f = 0x461c4000`, the squared 100 cut-off. No other distance constant in these functions.

**Rule (the port's, now shared):** a player is in the area of an enemy's Zalure or Jellen object when its XZ distance from the object is strictly less than `techReach(tech, level)` = `rangeH(tech, level) + 5`. The 5 is the player's hit box radius (`PLAYER_RADIUS`; the lobby note in this file: "the player's hitbox radius is 5 for every class"); the probe radius is `range_h`. Both techs use their own row (equal numbers today).

**Changes:**
- `client/src/combat/techfire.ts`: `inTechReach(tech, level, dist)` = `dist < techReach(tech, level)`, next to `techReach`.
- `client/src/combat/enemyfsmep2a.ts` (Gi Gue stomp): the same test through `inTechReach` (the old `>= reach` skip gave the same boundary).
- `client/src/combat/enemyfsmep2c.ts` (`SinowZoaAi.cast`): was `techData(TECH.jellen, level).rangeH` with `> range` for both objects (no +5, not strict). Now each object tests `inTechReach(TECH.zalure | TECH.jellen, level, dist)`: at level 4 the reach goes 50 -> 55, strict.
- `docs/DEVLOG.md`: a correction under "Technique visuals: Zonde, Grants, Megid, supports, special objects" (its Jellen `range_h` was wrong).

**Tests:**
- `tests/techfire.test.ts`: Jellen at level 4 just inside 55 and not 55; Zalure at level 10 just inside 79 and not 79.
- `tests/enemyfsmep2a.test.ts`: the stomp at level 4, a player 54.5 away is hit, one 55 away is not.
- `tests/enemyfsmep2c.test.ts` (Zele block): a player 54.5 from the Zele gets Jellen and Zalure, one 55 away gets neither.

**ASSUMED:** the overlap is read as a round test of XZ radius `range_h + 5` (the port's convention, as the Dark Falz objects and Razonde's `range_h + 5`); the `0xffff` argument of `0x006ded14` means no class boost (`techData(tech, level)` with charClass 0); the candidate order does not matter to the stomp, which takes every player in reach.

**UNCLEAR:** the shape of `0x007b5318` (it walks 11-dword hit-box records with flags at `+0x18` and calls float helpers `0x0082d990`, `0x0083a610`, `0x0082da80`, `0x0082ebac` that were not decoded), so whether the test is a true round shape or a box (a box of half width 5 reaches `range_h + 5 * sqrt(2)` on a diagonal), and the height test (`P+0xa8`, `P+0x60`); whether the edge is `<` or `<=` (the port: strict); the 8-slot list `0xaad6e0`; the `0x006eb354` variant's use. The Resta / Anti / Shifta / Deband / Reverser areas in the 2026-10-20 entry were not re-checked here.

## 2026-10-21: Saint-Milion explosion damage and laser path (read)

Two read-only Haiku passes; the decisive instructions were checked here. They correct the three Saint-Milion entries above.

**The explosion `0x0076a724`** (missile type 3, laser type 5) is a thiscall on `[0x00a9b07c]`, which is the **boss itself**: its ctor 0x0076a8e8 (vtable 0x00b43880, factory 0x0076a86c) stores `this` there at 0x0076a9e0; 0x007675fa clears it. Its +0x3d0 is the boss's EnemyMovementData row (the port's `row`), so 0x00768990's `fild [[boss+0x3d0]+0x20]` (type 3) / `+0x28` (type 5) is **iparam3 / iparam5**, stored as the damage float at out+4 (0x00768a54; out+0 = 0). The 3.0 (missile) / 10.0 (laser) that follow are a separate value passed on (knockback-like, meaning UNCLEAR), not a multiplier. The hit goes through the area-hit object `[0x00a72eb4]` (ctor 0x00521bbc, vtable 0x00b009a0, created at 0x00521950): a radius up to 100 takes the thunk 0x00521cdc, which calls vtable +0x30 (0x00521cf8) with **100.0** (0x00521cdc `push 0x42c80000`). The constants 0x009216cc..d4 (all 100.0) are compared with the radius, not with a height. The scan is XZ only (0x007a9180), no height test. 0x00521cf8 walks the 16-slot list 0x00aad6e0: an entity with word +0x96 == 1 (the port treats it as a player), not the attacker and without +0x30 & 0x4000000 is checked part by part (0x005221c0, hit boxes at +0xa4) and gets one `vtable +0x60(attacker, 0, damage, part, -1, -1)` per call. So: **missile = one explosion at its end, iparam3 to every player within 100 XZ; laser = iparam5 per frame with a target** (see below). UNCLEAR: the defender's +0x60 / +0x48 (defence, knockback), the list identities 0x00aad6e0 / 0x00aad720, the type 0 path.

**The laser beam** (ctor 0x0076cb9c, update 0x0076ccdc): origin O = the boss-node transform of a one-frame track sample at frame 29 (0x00579de0 on `[0x00a9b080 + 4k]`, track ctor 0x005795a0 called at 0x0076b4d5 with start = end = 29.0); the source of the sample data is UNCLEAR. Each frame P = O + R_owner (amp * sin θ, 0, rate * θ) (local x sideways, local z forward; table 0x009779b8 per type {step, rate, amp} = {728, 0.00213623, -140}, {728, 0.00213623, 140}, {280, 0.00717163, -300}, {280, 0.00717163, 300}), then θ += step: about 1.56 (types 0 / 1) or 2.01 (2 / 3) units forward a frame, a lateral period of 90 / 234 frames. The ramp +0x58 grows 0.025 a frame to 1.0. The hit test 0x00780630 checks P against each entity's **own** XZ circle (record +0x4 x, +0xc z, +0x10 r; 0x00780661..0x0078067c; mask 0x16ef), not a ramp radius; the selector 0x00780874 keeps one winner; with a winner the beam calls the explosion with type 5 and radius ramp * 64 (so the 100 scan applies). **With no winner the beam sets its dead bit (0x0076ce32)**: since the list 0x00aab3f0 apparently holds more than players (floor pieces?), what it really tests is UNCLEAR. The telegraph (ctor 0x00765c68, vtable 0x00b43410) lives for the phase-4 motion and calls the dispatcher with type 4 (iparam2 × 0) each frame its child slot 1 is flagged.

Earlier entries corrected: the missile's 3.0 is not a multiplier; there is no height window; the scan radius is 100 (not 30 or 64 * ramp); the laser's hit circle is the entity's. Not ported yet.

## 2026-10-21: Saint-Milion: the sine beam is the wave (state 21), not the laser

Correction of "Saint-Milion lasers" and of the laser part of "Saint-Milion explosion damage and laser path (read)" (a Haiku pass on the wave found it; checked here). States 19 / 20 use handler 0x007697dc, which only has a phase-4 branch: `cmp eax,4; jne; call 0x0076b85c` (the object with ctor 0x00765c68, vtable 0x00b43410 that those entries called the "telegraph"). State 21 uses 0x007697f0: phase 4 returns, phase 0 calls 0x00769808, the body that spawns the sine beam (ctor 0x0076cb9c, update 0x0076ccdc). So everything those entries say about the beam (frame 27 effect 0x6f9, frame 28 type choice by arena and a 0.5 roll, the frame-29 track origin, P = O + R(amp * sin θ, 0, rate * θ), the 0x009779b8 table, the ramp, the XZ-circle test against list 0xaab3f0 with mask 0x16ef, death on the first frame without a winner, the type-5 explosion with iparam5 each frame with a winner) describes the **wave**. The port's `case 21` emits its 'wave' event on entry (phase 4), where the exe does nothing; the beam appears at clock 28 of phase 0.

The **laser** of states 19 / 20 is therefore the 0x00765c68 object: it lives for the phase-4 motion (frames [boss+0xe98] - 1), spawns effect 0x6f8 once, recomputes an aim angle from its +0x44 vector each frame (0x0082f9c4 + fpatan) and, each frame its child slot 1 is flagged, calls the attack dispatcher 0x00768a84 with type 4 (`fild [row+0x1c]` = iparam2 with a 0 multiplier, then the common tail 0x00768a50). Its hit rule is UNCLEAR (not decoded yet).

Also from that pass: storm = state 23 (handler 0x007699ac; phase 4 -> 0x0076b7a8, base ctor 0x00766b20; phase 5 -> 0x0076a708); the table comment in saintmilionboss.ts that labels row 23 "cutscene" is wrong. ## 2026-10-21: Saint-Milion wave: its "hit test" is a ground probe

Follow-up of the two entries above (a Haiku pass; the decisive constants and counts were checked here). `0x00780630(P, mask)` is a generic collision probe, not a target test: it is called from 51 sites in the exe (`grep -cP "call\t0x780630 "`), mostly with mask 0x16ef. The list `[0x00aab3f0]` (created by 0x007a7c90 at area setup, about 12 init sites; null-terminated record pointers at list+0x20) holds **map collision objects**: records added by 0x007a7b30 from the ctor of the collision-object class (vtable 0x00b33580, ctor 0x0065f9e4; record at owner+0xac: +0 mesh, +4 / +8 / +0xc position, +0x10 radius, +0x14 flags) and by the City Door (vtable 0x00b2f880); no player or enemy is ever added. 0x00780630 keeps the records whose flags & mask and whose XZ circle contains P, then 0x00780874 traces a vertical probe from (P.x, P.y - 10000, P.z) (0x009798fc = -10000.0, t limit 0x00979900 = 2.0) through their polygons (word +6 & mask) and keeps the nearest hit. The result struct holds the hit fraction t at +4, not an entity id (the earlier "+4 = entity id" is wrong), and the beam does not use the winner for damage.

So the wave beam each frame: if the ground probe under P finds collision, it explodes there (type 5, iparam5 to every player within 100 XZ, every frame); if not, it sets its dead bit. In practice it runs along the arena floor and ends when it leaves it, ASSUMED that the arena's floor is among the registered collision objects (not proven). UNCLEAR: the flag bit meanings, a register oddity in 0x00780630's return path (0x007806c9), and the beam's removal after the dead bit (0x00765a40).

## 2026-10-21: Saint-Milion missiles ported

**Outcome: the missiles fly and explode now.** State 18 (row 18 of 0x009f6c60, handler 0x0076966c) launches real `SmMissile` shots instead of the event alone. The event `missiles` stays for the renderer. Built on the corrected reading of the last entry: the blast is iparam3 to the players within 100 on the XZ plane, not a height window or a radius of 30.

**What changed.**
- `combat/saintmilionents.ts`: `SmMissile` (an `EnemyShot`) and `SM_MISSILE = { speed: 5, life: 240, blast: 100, knockback: 3 }`.
- `combat/enemyshots.ts`: a new `ShotEffect` kind `blast` (a fixed damage, cause_knockback, no MST formula, no roll).
- `combat/saintmilionboss.ts`: `SM.missileFrame = 5`; state 18 phase 4 makes one missile (`launchMissiles(1)`), phase 0 makes two more on the clock's frame 5 in arenas 3 / 4 only (`missileFrame`, `arena` +0xf80). The damage is `row.iparam[2]` (iparam3) of the form being fought.
- `render/combat.ts`: `tickShots` routes a `blast` hit to `enemyBlastHitsPlayer`, which calls `damage.hit` on the local player like the group-0 tech hit does, with the value as the damage, and gains PB like it does.
- `tests/saintmilionboss.test.ts`: section 8 (entry and phase-0 counts per arena, 5.0 a frame, 240 frames, one blast within 100 on XZ, the living only, once).
- `docs/HANDOFF.md` item 4: "missiles" removed from the events-only list.

**Constants and addresses.**
- 0x00976174 = 5.0: the flight speed.
- `cmp [this+0x68], 0xf0` / `jg 0x766786` (in the update 0x007663d4): 240 frames; the port explodes when the count passes 240.
- 0x0076b8f4: phase 4 (one missile). 0x0076968c: phase 0, `call 0x7aaa30` with 5.0 (the clock's frame 5) and `cmp [+0xf80], 3 / 4`: two missiles.
- 0x00521cdc `push 0x42c80000` (100.0): the blast radius, the XZ scan of 0x007a9180 (no height test).

- Knockback 3.0 (`SM_MISSILE.knockback`): the value passed with the blast; its meaning is unclear.

**ASSUMED.**
- The flight is a straight line on flat ground, toward the nearest living player at launch (`FindNearestPlayer`), or along the heading if nobody is alive. The two phase-0 missiles aim at that same player.
- The end of the flight is the frame count: the motion's state 4 is not read. The blast happens at the end of the flight.
- **Conflict with the exe:** the 240-frame branch 0x00766786 reaches the kill 0x007667a8 without the explosion call (0x007667e4 is only on the motion-end path). The port explodes at 240 anyway, as the brief asked, because the port cannot see the motion end. If the exe's 240-frame end does not explode, the blast should move to the motion-end test.

- The missile is a ball drawn at height 10 (`look: orange, size 1.5`); the exe draws a model.
- The blast has no defence taken off; the knockback 3.0 goes to `damage.hit` as is.

## 2026-10-21: Saint-Milion wave ported

**What changed.** State 21 (the wave, 0x007697f0) now makes its beam. The phase-4 entry still only emits the 'wave' event (the exe does nothing there). On phase 0, one `SmWave` is pushed to `out.shots` on the clock's frame 28 (`SM.waveFrame`), through the same clock-crossing test the missile's frame 5 uses. The beam is a `blast` shot, so `render/combat.ts` `enemyBlastHitsPlayer` applies it with no change there.
- `client/src/combat/saintmilionents.ts`: `SM_WAVE` (the table, ramp step, radius, knockback, height, life) and `SmWave extends EnemyShot`.
- `client/src/combat/saintmilionboss.ts`: `waveFrame()` in phase 0 of `case 21`, `SM.waveFrame: 28`, a table comment fix (row 23 is the storm, not a cutscene), and the header list no longer names the wave as events only.
- `tests/saintmilionboss.test.ts`: section 9.
- `docs/HANDOFF.md` item 4: "wave" removed from the events-only list.

**Rules.**
- Type (0x009773c8): arena 3 / 4 -> base 2, the others -> base 0; `+1` when `rand.float() >= 0.5` (the higher type). The roll is the boss's own `SmRng`.
- Table 0x009779b8, per type {step (BAMS a frame), rate, amp}: t0 {728, 0.00213623046875, -140}, t1 {728, 0.00213623046875, 140}, t2 {280, 0.007171630859375, -300}, t3 {280, 0.007171630859375, 300}.
- Each frame: P = O + R(amp * sin θ, 0, rate * θ), θ in BAMS (65536 = 360 degrees; x sideways, z forward), then θ += step, ramp = min(1, ramp + 0.025). θ starts at 0, so the first frame's P is O. R turns the local frame by the heading, with forward = (sin, cos) as in the missile.
- Hit: the ground probe under P. With ground, an explosion of type 5 at P: `iparam5` (`row.iparam[4]`, the form's row) to every living player within 100 on XZ (`<= 100`, no height test), every frame, no once-per-player gate, knockback 10.0. Without ground, the beam is done on that frame, with no hit.
- The effect 0x6f9 at frame 27 is not drawn, so nothing is pushed for it.

**Constants and addresses.**
- 0x00769808 (phase 0 of state 21), 0x007aaa30 (the clock's crossing test), 0x009773c8 (the type roll), 0x009779b8 (the table), 0x0076cb9c / 0x0076ccdc (the beam's ctor / update).
- The ramp 0.025 is the `+0x58` step; the exe's ramp scales a radius of ramp * 64 in the old reading, which is superseded: the blast is the 100 scan (0x00521cdc), so `ramp` is kept but no hit uses it.

**ASSUMED.**
- **Origin O:** the boss's position at the spawn, and the heading at spawn is the beam's frame. The exe's origin is a boss node at frame 29 of a one-frame track whose data is not read, so this is wrong by the node's offset.
- **Height:** the beam is drawn at 10 (`SM_WAVE.height`); nothing reads it for the hit.
- **End:** the probe is the boss's `ground` callback (`ground(x, z, 60) !== null` in render/combat.ts) when it has one. Without it, the beam's floor is the boss's arena circle (`SM_ARENAS[arena]`: origin and range; arenas 3 / 4 use (0, 0) and 620). The exe's collision probe (0x00780630 / 0x00780874) tests map collision objects, and the port cannot reproduce that exactly, so the callback is the closest stand-in.
- **Life cap:** 600 frames (`SM_WAVE.life`); the exe's beam has no cap that was read.
- **Knockback** 10.0 is the value the exe passes with type 5. Its meaning is unknown, as the missile's 3.0 is.
- **Look:** a coloured ball per frame at P (0x60c0ff, size 1). The exe draws a model, which is not ported.

**Checks.**
- `node tests/saintmilionboss.test.ts`: ALL PASS (section 9: entry emits 'wave' but no beam; one beam at the clock's crossing of 28; type by arena for 40 seeds, both types in each pair, and the higher type when the roll is >= 0.5; P for frames 0 .. 3 for t0 at heading 0 and t2 at 0x4000, exact to 1e-9; ramp; iparam5 to the living within 100 on frames 1 and 2 with the edge in and the far and the dead out; no ground ends the beam with no hit; the 600-frame cap; the arena circle ends it).
- `node tests/saintmilion.test.ts`: all checks passed.
- `node tests/combat.test.ts`: 5946 checks, 0 failures.
- `client`: `tsc --noEmit` clean (Node 24).

Not run in Chrome.

## 2026-10-21: classic party create / join enter the game

**Bug** (user: creating and joining a party still did not work; a created party must open the loading screen, not stay on the map). Reproduced with Playwright against the local newserv:
- **Create:** C1 and the 64 worked, then `partyHost.back` (classic/main.ts) sent 98 / 84 at once and showed the lobby again ("the classic field is not implemented, back to the lobby"): by design since 2026-10-19, there was no field on the classic page.
- **Join:** 10 and the 64 worked against a game held by a client that had finished loading (a script), and the joiner was then sent back to the lobby the same way. Between two classic clients a join could not work: the creator left its game at once (newserv deleted it), and a creator that stays without loading (no 6F) makes newserv refuse every join with "You cannot join this game because another player is currently loading. Try again soon." (checked with a held game that never sent 6F).
- **Idle drop:** the classic lobby never sent anything while the player only stood or read the counter's menus, and `net/lobby.ts` does not answer 1D; newserv's `ClientIdleTimeout` (60 s, `Client.cc` "Idle timeout expired") then dropped the connection, so the list / create / join of a player who took a minute at the counter failed. Seen live: idle 75 s in the lobby on the unchanged client (5173) logs "[classic] disconnected from the lobby server" and newserv "Idle timeout expired"; with this change (5174) no disconnect.

**What the exe does after the 64** (Ephinea `PsoBB.exe`, objdump; the dump's names in brackets):
- `handle_packet0x64` (ends 0x0079c018) sets the next floor to 0 (`SetFloorAndMapVariant` 0x00815590 on the floor block 0x00ac9d4c, `mov ecx, 0xac9d4c` at 0x0079bff5), calls 0x007bd788 (`or` 1 into 0x00aae6d0 and into the floor flags 0x00ac9d6c = block + 0x20) and 0x007a6114 (`is_loading_screen_showing = 1`, 0x00aab380).
- The logged-in game loop (`GameLoop_Update` 0x007bcc4c, which also runs the lobby) sees the flag and calls `play_loading_screen_animation(floor)` (0x00417a9c). For type 2 it calls `get_warp_type` (0x00815648) on the floor block: previous floor > 0x11 -> 4, bit 0 of +0x20 -> 2, else 0 / 1 by the floor order (Vol Opt special case). 0x00417a9c maps 0 -> floor_prev (3), 1 -> floor_next (4), anything else -> lobby (0). So a game entry shows the **lobby** loading screen: `update_loading_screen_widget` (0x00417ccc) builds `create_lobby_burst_screen` on its second frame, i.e. the warp of `classic/connecting.ts`, under the root's fade-in (`GameListWindowObjectConstructor` creates the 0x00af2620 fade object, mode 2), without the "Connecting.." object (FUN_00407b74 belongs to the connect loop only).
- Behind it the floor loads; `call_map_initializer`, `unk_end_loading_screen`, then 6x23 and the rest; `ClearLobbyFlagIfNotLobby` (0x008156b0) clears the bit once the map is not a lobby.
- `ping_server` (0x007bd288, called at 0x007bccda by the game loop and at 0x007bd3a0): while logged in, 1D every 900 frames (`g_FrameCounter % 900`, the 0x91a2b3c5 division).

**What changed:**
- `classic/main.ts`: the party host's join / create resolve on the 64 and start `enterGame`: the loading screen (`ConnectingScreen` with `{ status: false }`) covers the window, the lobby view is disposed, the Online tab's `GameView` loads Pioneer 2 on the 3D canvas (6x3F / 6x1F / 6x3B / 6x23 / 6F as there), then `classic/field.ts` (`FieldScreen`) is shown. The lobby teleporter (`GameView.onLobbyWarp`) or a failed load (its message on the loading screen, Enter) goes through `leaveGame`: 98 / 84 and the lobby. The game name of a join comes from the list entry until 8A brings it. Hooks: `classicGame`, `classicGameLoading`; `classicLobby` is cleared while in a game.
- `classic/field.ts` (new): a transparent stage screen that forwards the stage canvas's keys (and the touch pad's / soft keyboard's, which go to it) to the 3D canvas, where the field's movement, combat, item and menu listeners are; sends `ping_server`'s 1D.
- `classic/connecting.ts`: `ConnectingOptions.status` (false: no "Connecting.." text, no 150-frame wait; the screen ends with the load).
- `classic/lobby.ts`: `PING_FRAMES` = 900, 1D from the lobby screen's frame counter.
- The stream file: the game connection answers 04EB / 03EB in about 6 s here (login connection: 18 ms), which held the floor load (combat waits for the battle params) for 13 s. The classic page now reads it on the login connection right after login (the exe gets it there too) and hands it to `GameView` / `CombatView` (`streamFiles` option; the game connection is still asked when it is missing or failed). Loading Pioneer 2 went from 15-28 s to about 3 s in the test.
- `GameView` option `labels: false` (no name sprites over the players on the classic page; the classic lobby already passes it to `LobbyView`).
- `net/game.ts` `leave`: 30 s instead of 8 s for the 67. With two headless clients rendering and newserv's command logging, newserv read the 84 up to 11 s after the 98 (its E7 send in between), and one e2e run timed out.

**ASSUMED:** the lobby type's music (`PlayLoadingScreenMusic(0)`) is not played (the screen stops the BGM like the connect warp); the fade-in and particles are the connect warp's; a load error waits for Enter on the loading screen and then leaves the game (the exe has no such path); the 1D counter restarts with each screen instead of the global `g_FrameCounter`; leaving the game shows no loading screen (`unknown_init_lobby` also calls `play_loading_screen_animation(floor)`; which screen that picks was not traced).

**Not on the classic page yet** (the Online tab has them): the Pioneer 2 NPC talk, counters and quests (`quest/town.ts`, `net/quests.ts`), the chat line in games, the mouse in the field (the 3D canvas takes no pointer events under the stage).

**Checks:** Playwright (`PW_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:5174`, a worktree Vite): `e2e/party-create.spec.ts` (create, loading screen, Pioneer 2 loaded and 6F sent, no lobby, back to the lobby) and the new `e2e/party-join.spec.ts` (two contexts: A creates at the counter and enters, B joins from the list, both see two players, both leave): `--repeat-each=3` 6 passed; after the last code change `--repeat-each=2` 4 passed (create 33.3 s / 23.8 s, join 57.0 s / 53.2 s) and a plain run 2 passed (create 24.0 s, join 50.9 s). A screenshot run showed the warp during the load and Pioneer 2 with the field HUD, W moved the player (keys forwarded). `tests/gamelist.live.ts`, `tests/game.live.ts` pass; `tests/gamelist`, `combat`, `combatdepth` and the other 23 tests that import the touched modules pass; client `tsc --noEmit` clean. Not checked by hand in Chrome.

## 2026-10-21: Saint-Milion laser: the beam test (read), aim source still unknown

Follow-up of the laser paragraph above (a Haiku pass; the spawn copy was checked here). **0x00772c08(player, laser)** is a sector test: in a frame translated by -laser.pos and rotated by the player's heading, each hit box of the player (list +0xa4, count +0xa8, stride 0x2c; boxes with +0x18 & 0x02000000 skipped; centre +0..+8, radius +0xc) passes when its horizontal distance is below box.r + L and |atan2(x, z) (BAMS) - laser heading| is below the half-span; y is ignored. 0x00768a84 sets those values in the record laser+0x31c for the loop only: L (+0x8) = the horizontal length origin (+0x38) -> aim point (+0x44), the span (+0xc) = |previous aim angle (+0x58) - this frame's aim angle|, and the heading +0x60 = their midpoint (0x007a8cb8); all are restored on exit. So the laser **sweeps**: each flagged frame it hits the players inside the wedge between the last frame's and this frame's aim direction, out to the aim point's distance, when the line of sight is clear (0x77fffc), with iparam2 through the player's vtable +0x60.

**Aim source: UNCLEAR.** The spawn 0x007679d0 copies the origin into the aim point (0x00767a00..0x00767a09: +0x44..+0x4c = +0x38..+0x40, checked), and nothing in the laser's own code (ctor 0x00765c68, update 0x00765d7c, draw 0x00765ed8) writes +0x44 again. Read literally the wedge would have zero length and span and never hit, which does not fit the game, so something else moves the aim point (the boss's motion through the laser's child objects, or a generic writer: not found among the many `[reg+0x44]` stores). Other laser spawners: 0x00767962 (tables 0x009f75f4 / 0x009f7630 by arena), 0x0076b1ff, 0x0076ba60. The flagged-frame window (child slot 1, +0x9c bit 2) comes from motion data. Not ported.

## 2026-10-21: Saint-Milion storm and sand sonic ported

**What changed.**
- `combat/saintmilionents.ts`: `SmBlast` (an `EnemyShot`, one explosion: the living players within max(r, 100) on XZ, once; the `blast` effect), `SM_STORM` / `SmStorm` (a plain object the boss keeps; four explosions), `SM_SAND` / `SmSandSonic` (an `EnemyShot`: waits, launches, 20 moves, one explosion per move).
- `combat/saintmilionboss.ts`: state 23 phase 4 makes the storm (centre: the arena's origin, `SM_ARENAS[arena]`; damage iparam4 = `row.iparam[3]`); the storm is ticked on every boss frame. State 10 at the clock's 45 still emits 'sandsonic' and makes the sand sonic, which joins `out.shots` on its launch frame. New option `atp` (the boss's base ATP).
- `render/combat.ts`: the boss gets `atp: attacker?.atp` (the stats row's ATP before Jellen).
- `tests/saintmilionboss.test.ts`: sections 10 (storm) and 11 (sand sonic).
- `docs/HANDOFF.md` item 4: storm and sand sonic are off the events-only list (lasers stay).

**Rules and constants.**
- Storm: T = 75 n (0x00976234 = 75.0), n = 1 on the first frame. Radii 100, 200, 400, 1000 (0x00976224 .. 0x00976230). The explosion of radius r goes off on the frame T first passes r (r < T <= r + 75): frames 2, 3, 6 and 14, then it ends.
- Storm damage: trunc(f32(iparam4 * factor)) with the factors of types 6 .. 9 of the damage dispatcher 0x00768990 (jump table 0x009768c4): 1.0, 0.8, 0.64, 0.32 (the products of 0x0097748c, 0x00977484 and 0x00977488 = 0.5, which is an intermediate of type 9). Knockback 3.0 (0x40400000 on every type).
- Sand sonic: made at the clock's 45 (state 10, phase 0), waits trunc(6 * rng) frames (0x009774ac = 6.0) with the boss's `SmRng`. Launch (0x0076c974): start = node 0x17 (the exe adds 100 to its height and snaps it to the ground), heading = atan2 of node 4 -> node 0x17 in XZ. Then 20 moves (+0xb4 = 0x14) of 10.0 (+0xb0 = 0x41200000) along the heading, removed after the 20th.
- Each move explodes once at its position (0x0076c4ec -> 0x0076a788, type 2): damage = the base ATP, the int16 at [boss+0x2c4] (type 2 of 0x00768990 reads `movsx [ecx+0x2c4]`); knockback = 10.0 x 1.01 (0x00977940) = 10.1, the third argument; radius = d * 120 * g (the fourth argument, 0x0097793c = 120.0), with g the runtime global [0xa9b0a4].
- d: the XZ distance from node 4 to the sand sonic. The point node 4 is written at +0xbc at the launch, and 0x0076c548 takes |(+0xbc) - (+0x38)| in XZ. So d is measured from node 4, not from the launch point (the earlier read said the same).

**ASSUMED.**
- Storm: active from its creation (the exe gates its update on a motion flag, not readable); it runs whatever the boss's state. Centre = `SM_ARENAS[arena]` origin (ox, oz); the exe's centre is the runtime global [0x00a9b020], not decoded.
- Sand sonic: g = π / 720 (the runtime global [0x00a9b0a4] is not readable), so the radius is d * π / 6 (at least 100).
- Start: node 0x17 without the +100 height and the ground snap (the port's sand sonic is at height 0). Without node data the launch is from the boss position along `swingAngle`.
- The heading uses the fresh node positions at the launch (the same value as `swingAngle` when the nodes are known).
- The timing: the wait counts boss frames; the sand sonic joins the shots on the frame it launches and its first move is its first shot tick (the renderer's), then one move and one explosion per tick.
- Knockback 10.1: the exe's value; its meaning is not known (as the missile's 3.0).
- The explosions are hidden (not drawn); the exe's effects (0x6f7, 0x6fc, 0x6fd) are not ported. The sand sonic is drawn as a ball at its position.
- No defence is taken off a blast; each client resolves its own hit (as for the missile).

## 2026-10-21: Saint-Milion laser: correction, 0x007679d0 is the boss's, not the laser's

Correction of "Saint-Milion laser: the beam test (read), aim source still unknown" (a Haiku pass found it; checked here). 0x007679d0 is called with the **boss** as `this`: its caller 0x00767940 starts `mov ebp, ecx; mov edx, [ebp+0xf80]` (the arena index) and passes `ecx = ebp` to 0x007679d0 at 0x00767962; the other callers (0x0076b1ff, 0x0076ba60) pass the same boss-class `this`. So the stores at 0x00767a00..0x00767a09 set the boss's own +0x44..+0x4c = +0x38..+0x40 (its position, snapped by 0x007b4c58), not a laser's aim point; that entry's "the spawn copies the origin into the aim point" is wrong.

What stands: the laser (ctor 0x00765c68, only built by 0x0076b85c from the state-19 handler 0x007697dc; the boss keeps no pointer to it) never writes its own +0x38 / +0x44 (update 0x00765d7c only reads them at 0x00765daf..0x00765dbb), its base and ctor do not set them, and its child tracks (table 0x009f5a9c = {0, 3, 5}, factory 0x00661448 / 0x006614cc, vtable 0x00b33970, update 0x00660f68) write their own target node, not the laser. The nearest lead is 0x007657f8(slot, vec) called from 0x007663b0 in 0x00766384, which copies a position from `[[this+0x60]+0x30..0x38]` into a child: a different object family, not tied to the laser yet. **Who sets the laser's origin and aim each frame is still unknown**; the laser stays unported (a port would need an ASSUMED aim, e.g. a sweep from the boss's heading).

## 2026-10-21: classic: loading screen when leaving a game

**Question:** the lobby teleporter (or a failed load) returned to the lobby with no loading screen. What does the exe show when a game is left? Read from the reference dump (`refsrc/original-psobb-client-source/src/Psobb.exe-05112026.c`, function names as the dump gives them; the exe's addresses where the dump names them).

**Exe path (read):**
- The Pioneer 2 lobby teleporter: `unknown_handle_lobby_warp_list` (dump line 535707) -> `change_lobby_through_warp_menu` (782831): sends 84 with the lobby number and sets `g_CurrentLobbyMenuId = unknown_burst` (19). It does not set `g_IsLeavingParty`.
- The 67 (lobby join): `HandleLobbyJoinPartyState_0079c070` (780182) is the 0x67 callback. It sets the lobby state (menu 1) and the lobby objects, and calls no loading screen.
- The 98 (character save on leaving): `SendLobbySyncPacket_0079f900` (783001), called only from `unknown_init_lobby` (805727).
- `unknown_init_lobby` is the lobby entry. `GameLoop_Update_007bcc4c` (0x007bcc4c) calls it when `g_IsLeavingParty == 1` (805444); a quest end calls it too (805690). `g_IsLeavingParty` is set by `CheckPlayerLeaveStateAndPlaySound_0064af24` (512287, sound 6; no direct caller found by xref), by the quest state 3 `SinowberillChallengeEntity_UpdateState3_006ad954` (600027) and by `HandlePartyLeaderUpdate_007a0d84` (784204) when the menu is party_burst. **UNCLEAR:** which of these the teleporter path reaches; the 84 path alone does not set it.
- `unknown_init_lobby` calls `MapStateTransitionHandler_008155a8` (prev = the game floor, cur = the target), then `play_loading_screen_animation(floor)` (805763) before it loads the lobby floor (0xf / 0x10).
- `play_loading_screen_animation` (156869) maps `floor` through `get_warp_type` (833294): previous floor > 0x11 -> 4 (-> lobby); floor flag bit 0 (+0x20) -> 2 (-> lobby); else 0 (-> floor_prev) or 1 (-> floor_next) by the floor order (Vol Opt special case).
- `update_loading_screen_widget` (157007) builds by type: lobby -> `create_lobby_burst_screen` (the warp of `classic/connecting.ts`); quest -> `QuestLoadingScreenConstructor` (`classic/questloading.ts`); floor_prev / floor_next -> `GameListObjectConstructor` (a 0x1c-byte object, the floor warp, with `g_ChallengeListWindowFlag` for next).
- `ClearLobbyFlagIfNotLobby_008156b0` (833329) clears bit 0 once the current map is not a lobby. Where it is called was not traced.

**Result:** a leave from a game most likely shows the floor warp (floor_prev / floor_next, `GameListObjectConstructor`), not the lobby burst: during a game bit 0 is normally clear, so `get_warp_type` falls to the floor order. **UNCLEAR:** the sign of `[3] - cur` at that call (which decides prev or next), and whether `ClearLobbyFlagIfNotLobby` has run by then. The port has no equivalent of the floor warp object: `connecting.ts` is the lobby burst, `questloading.ts` the quest screen, `loadprogress.ts` the start-up bar.

**Change (as the brief asked, the lobby burst):**
- `classic/main.ts`: `leaveGame` shows `ConnectingScreen` with `{ status: false }` (as `enterGame` does) while `game.leave()` (98 / 84 / 67) runs and the lobby is built behind it; the lobby is shown when the burst is done. `enterLobby` is split into `buildLobby` (the screen, not shown), `showLobby` (the window hooks and `show`) and the same `showWorld(true)` as before. A failed leave shows its message on the loading screen; Enter logs it (the old code only logged; **ASSUMED**: the screen then stays black).
- If the exe's leave is the floor warp, change the screen type in `leaveGame` (`ConnectingScreen` -> a floor-warp screen) and not the 98 / 84 path; that screen does not exist in the port yet.
- `e2e/party-create.spec.ts`: the return step now runs the teleporter and checks that the loading screen was shown (sampled every 10 ms in the page, since the 98 / 84 is quick) before the lobby is up. The `leaveToLobby` import is dropped from that spec (`classic.ts` keeps the helper for `party-join.spec.ts`).

- The pushes at 0x00558d7e (0x2d4), 0x00558dcc (0x2d5), 0x00558ded and 0x00558ef5 (0x2d4), 0x00559c1a (0x2d2) and 0x00559cf4 (0x2d3) are the first arguments of 0x008144b0 = play_directional_sound_effect(id, pos, volume, param4) (dump line 832038) and 0x00814298 (the SE player, FUN_00814298 in tools/gen-se-tables.py). ## 2026-10-21: De Rol Le segment hit tint and beam particles

**What changed:** the 2026-10-20 "not reproduced" items of De Rol Le are done in part. (1) The segment plates take the hit flash: `combat/derolle.ts` already had the colour (`DrlSegment.color`); the body is one skinned mesh, so `render/njcmmesh.ts` gained `NjcmPartInput.ownMaterials` (opt-in): the strips of the listed nodes get materials of their own, tagged `userData.node`. A strip belongs to the node that caches it (a `cache` op keeps its owner, a `draw` in another node does not move it). `render/enemymodel.ts` passes it through `EnemyPartSpec.ownMaterials`, and `formats/enemymodels.ts` sets it on the De Rol Le body to draw nodes 1 + 2i (the plates). Each frame `render/combat.ts` (`syncDeRolLeSegments`) writes `DrlSegment.color` into those materials' colour (`setPlateDiffuse`), as the exe writes the node's diffuse. (2) The beam spawns its particles through `FieldParticles`: `DRL_BEAM` (`combat/derolle.ts`) is 0x126 at the start, 0x177 as a looping emitter that follows the muzzle while `beamFiring` is set, and 0x176 at the beam's end on every firing frame. Damage is untouched; the events are `particle` (0x126, 0x176) and the new `beamStart`.

**The exe (PsoBB.exe, read with objdump and exedata).**
- The segment colour is the function at **0x00435340**, not 0x00435334 (0x00435334 is a call inside the update, 0x00435294). It is called from the update at 0x00435302. The constants: `t = +0x3b0`; `t <= 0` gives white (0xffffffff); else the colour is ARGB with `a = 255 t` and `b = 255 (1 - t)`: R = b, G = B = a + b = 255 (the mix of the flash colour (0, 1, 1), written by the hit at 0x004354ea..0x00435516 as +0x3b8 = 0, +0x3bc = 1, +0x3c0 = 1, with white (1, 1, 1) at 0x008fd4cc..d4), then `t -= 0.05` (0x008fd4c4). So the flash starts cyan (0xff00ffff) and fades back to white in 20 frames: this is what `DrlSegment.tickColor` already does, and its tests (section 21b) pin it.
- The hit (0x004354c4): not broken: `+0x3b0 = 1` (the flash), then the pool `-= damage` (0x39c), and at 0 the break (vtable +0x1a8 = 0x004350d4) runs. Matches the port.
- The plate's material: `DerolleSetAnimationSpeed` (0x004355bc) writes the node's diffuse dword (`[+0x3a0]`, the node DAT_00a43c0c[i]) = `+0x3a8` (the whole ARGB; white when idle). Broken: the diffuse is 0 and the child (node 2 + 2i, `+0x3a4`) takes the colour's alpha (0), so the plate is invisible; the port still scales the two nodes down to hide them (unchanged, ASSUMED alpha 0 draws nothing).
- Real model (`bm_boss2_de_rol_le.bml`, body 176 nodes): nodes 1, 3, ... 23 have no vertices; their strips are `cache` / `draw` polys whose vertices are written by nodes 25 and up. So the plate's strips are polled by the plate node (cache) and drawn later, which is why the owner is the caching node. The plates' diffuse state is 0xffffffff (white), the children's ff ff ff 00.
- The beam is the state 0x1b handler, the function at **0x0042f96c** (its argument is the sub-phase, `cmp eax, 4`). The jump table at 0x00433cc0 (entry 0x1b at 0x008fcb6c) calls it from 0x00433d25.
